threatLevel: Elevated, multiple active PLC and perimeter device threats
executiveSummary: CISA warns that threat actors are actively probing and writing to Siemens S7 PLCs across U.S. critical infrastructure using S7comm tooling, with potential process safety impact. View Article Separate multi-agency guidance details Iranian-affiliated exploitation of internet-exposed PLCs (Rockwell, Schneider, Siemens), including logic tampering and alarm suppression. Immediate removal from internet, MFA-protected remote access, and logic integrity checks are urged. View Article Edge infrastructure risk remains acute: MikroTik RouterOS zero-days are under active exploitation for unauthenticated SSH takeover; patch immediately and assume compromise where SSH was exposed. View Article JPCERT/CC flags widespread availability of leaked Fortinet FortiGate credentials ("FortiBleed"), enabling perimeter breach and AD pivoting via site-to-site VPN trust; rotate creds, enforce PBKDF2, enable MFA, and audit for lateral movement. View Article Schneider Electric advisory (via CISA) confirms a session-hijacking flaw across Easergy/PowerLogic/Saitel and EcoStruxure Power components used in substations; patches available for many models-prioritize segmentation and session hardening. Security Advisory Multiple CISA weekly bulletins enumerate high-impact OT/ICS issues (OPC UA/Milo, smart meters, EVSE, DAQ/HMI platforms). Rapid patching, DPI controls on industrial protocols, and strong access control at OT perimeters are recommended. Supporting Report Supporting Report Berlin ransomware leak (Rhysida) published 5.7 TB including sensitive water/power substation and emergency plans-no ongoing cyber intrusion indicated, but physical and cyber-physical risks are elevated by exposed blueprints. relevance: Multiple, concurrent threat streams materially elevate near-term OT risk. Two joint U.S. government advisories document active PLC targeting and logic manipulation, spanning Siemens, Rockwell, and Schneider controllers. Simultaneously, widely deployed perimeter devices (MikroTik, Fortinet) are vulnerable or actively exploited, enabling rapid ingress and pivoting to OT jump hosts. ICS protocol/stack issues (OPC UA server/client; OPC UA LDS installers) and OT vendor flaws (Schneider Easergy/PowerLogic, PcVue, Ignition) increase the likelihood of unauthorized method execution, session hijacking, and operational disruption. The Berlin data leak adds non-cyber dimensions by exposing sensitive site blueprints, increasing the risk of blended threats.
